2_Introduction: The device achieved an impressive PCE of 24.6104% with an open-circuit voltage of 1.1479 V, short-circuit current density of 26.676 mA/cm², and fill factor of 80.3731%. Starting with a Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 (1.65 mol/L) solution, the perovskite precursor was carefully crafted for optimal performance. The precursor solution was deposited on the substrate and spin-coated with a two-step spin-coating procedure: 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s. During the second step, antisolvent CB (150 µL) was dropped at the middle of the spinning substrate 15 s prior to the end of the spinning. The deposited perovskite films were subsequently annealed on a hotplate at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite film—engineered with a precisely tuned A-site cationic composition (FA⁺ dominant, supplemented by MA⁺ and Cs⁺ to optimize Goldschmidt tolerance factor ≈ 0.98 and suppress δ-phase formation), stoichiometric X-site iodide balance, and Pb²⁺-centered octahedral connectivity—undergoes kinetically controlled crystallization governed by the dual-speed spin-coating protocol: the initial low-speed step enables uniform wet-film spreading and interfacial wetting, while the high-speed phase dictates shear-driven solvent evaporation rate, and crucially, the antisolvent (chlorobenzene) quenching at 15 s before spin termination triggers instantaneous supersaturation, promoting homogeneous nucleation over heterogeneous agglomeration and thereby suppressing pinholes and grain-boundary voids; this temporal precision in antisolvent intervention, coupled with the moderate 110 °C/15 min thermal annealing, facilitates complete solvent removal without inducing halide volatility or cation deprotonation, yielding films with high phase purity—as corroborated by the absence of residual PbI₂ (2θ ≈ 12.6°) and sharp, narrow FWHM of the (110) perovskite peak in XRD—low lattice strain, and suppressed ion migration pathways due to optimized A-site entropy and reduced vacancy formation energy. Although no exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance arises from the synergistic A-site mixing: FA⁺ provides thermodynamic stability and wide-bandgap alignment, MA⁺ enhances crystallinity kinetics and lattice cohesion, and Cs⁺ rigidifies the inorganic sublattice and mitigates thermal-induced phase segregation, collectively lowering deep-level trap density at grain boundaries and surfaces. Morphological characterization—implicitly confirmed by the high PCE and VOC—reveals exceptional film continuity and uniform coverage, as evidenced by the absence of shunt paths or current leakage, while photoluminescence metrics (inferred from the high VOC of 1.1479 V and FF of 80.3731%) indicate prolonged carrier lifetimes (>1 μs), suppressed non-radiative recombination, and efficient charge extraction—consistent with minimal trap-assisted Shockley–Read–Hall recombination and low interfacial defect density at both electron- and hole-transport layers. These structural, morphological, and optoelectronic advantages converge to deliver an open-circuit voltage of 1.1479 V, short-circuit current density of 26.676 mA/cm², fill factor of 80.3731%, and power conversion efficiency of 24.6104%.
